**Status: complete.** All nine parts of the template are written, adapted for a tool.

::: {.callout-note}
## D6 at a glance

- **A tool, not a model:** pricing estimates nothing. It is arithmetic on the scorecard's PD
  and seven market assumptions ([D0](../d0-summary.qmd#why-pricing-is-listed-as-a-tool-not-a-model)),
  and the arithmetic holds to within {{< var pricing.test_tolerance >}} on every booked loan
  ([6.5](performance.qmd)).
- **The headline:** {{< var pricing.share_clears >}} of the {{< var pricing.n >}} booked loans
  clear the {{< var market.roe_hurdle >}} ROE hurdle at the rate they were quoted; median ROE
  {{< var pricing.median_roe >}}; mispriced EAD \${{< var pricing.mispriced_ead >}} of
  \${{< var pricing.total_ead >}}.
- **What the headline measures:** the generator quotes each loan without the
  {{< var pricing.capital_charge >}} capital charge the hurdle needs, so most of the book
  misses it by construction. The share is a test of the measure on synthetic quotes, not a
  finding about any pricing practice (finding 1, [6.7](limitations.qmd)).
- **Loss-making at its own quote:** {{< var pricing.below_break_even.n >}} loans
  ({{< var pricing.below_break_even.share >}}) are quoted below break-even, and the tool's
  summary does not show them (finding 2).
- **One assumption dominates:** a {{< var pricing.sens.step >}} move in
  `{{< var pricing.sens.dominant >}}` moves the share clearing from
  {{< var pricing.share_clears >}} to between {{< var pricing.sens.cost_of_funds.up.share_clears >}}
  and {{< var pricing.sens.cost_of_funds.down.share_clears >}} ([6.6](sensitivity.qmd)).
- **Five open findings** the chapter raises about the tool and its inputs
  ([6.7](limitations.qmd)).
:::

Pricing answers two questions for every booked loan: **what rate would clear the bank's
return hurdle, and was the loan quoted below it?** ([6.1](purpose.qmd)). It takes the PD
from the Business Credit Score ([D4](../score/index.qmd), [D3](../d3-dependencies.qmd)), the
loan's exposure, the rate the loan was quoted and the market assumptions in
`shared.config.MARKET`, and runs a one-period profit waterfall
([6.3](methodology.qmd)). It is inventoried as a deterministic calculation tool, not a
model ([D0](../d0-summary.qmd#risk-tiering)): it has no estimated parameters. It still gets
a chapter, because its output drives decisions and its inputs need governing.

{{< include ../../_generated/pricing-headline.md >}}

Measured on the booked book: the {{< var pricing.n >}} loans the bank booked, each priced with
the scorecard's PD, its requested amount as EAD and the rate it was quoted
([6.2](data.qmd)). Every number in the chapter is a named fact, recomputed through the
module's own functions — `price_population`, `portfolio_summary` and the engine in
`pricing/src/engine.py` — by `python verify.py`; the [fact index](../../reference/facts.qmd)
gives each one's source and population. The chapter documents the tool as committed: it
changes neither the engine nor the assumptions.

## How the template is adapted for a tool

The nine-part [template](../index.qmd#the-template) was written for models: parts 5, 6 and
9 assume estimated parameters, a performance to measure and a statistical gate. Pricing has
none of the three. Each part is kept, in the same place, and answers the question a
validator would ask of a tool instead:

| Template part | For a model | Here, for a tool | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 Performance | discrimination, calibration, stability | **Accuracy and outcomes**: the arithmetic identities over the whole book, the what-if equal to the batch, and the outcome the tool reports | There is nothing estimated to be accurate *about*. What can be wrong is the arithmetic, the implementation that serves it, and how its output is read. |
| 6 Sensitivity | refits on reduced inputs | each market assumption moved by {{< var pricing.sens.step >}}, and the PD scaled | The tool's output moves only when an input does; the inputs are where its risk lives. |
| 9 Gate record | a committed metric minimum | **Controls in place of a gate**: unit tests, the facts' identity checks, `verify.py`'s summary comparison and the what-if tests | A tool has no metric to gate; it has invariants to assert. |

The other six parts keep their questions. Methodology has no fitting step, so it documents
the formula and the choices in it; Assumptions covers the market values and the
simplifications in the waterfall; Limitations, Monitoring and Purpose read as for a model.

| § | Part | What it establishes |
|---|---|---|
| 6.1 | [Purpose and use](purpose.qmd) | the hurdle-clearing rate, the mispricing measure, the consumers, prohibited uses |
| 6.2 | [Data and inputs](data.qmd) | the booked book, the score's PD, EAD, the quoted rate and why reading it is not leakage |
| 6.3 | [Methodology](methodology.qmd) | the profit waterfall step by step on one loan; break-even, hurdle-clearing and recommended rates |
| 6.4 | [Assumptions](assumptions.qmd) | each market value, what it means and who should own it; the simplifications |
| 6.5 | [Accuracy and outcomes](performance.qmd) | identities, what-if equals batch, the headline, mispricing by band and industry |
| 6.6 | [Sensitivity](sensitivity.qmd) | each assumption ±{{< var pricing.sens.step >}}; PD scaled, and why it equals LGD |
| 6.7 | [Limitations and compensating controls](limitations.qmd) | five open findings, each with a control and an owner |
| 6.8 | [Monitoring plan](monitoring.qmd) | book shares, mispricing by band, the assumption change log |
| 6.9 | [Controls in place of a gate](gate.qmd) | the tests and checks that stand in for a gate, and their history |
